expectations.text: Output produces an execution-ready or launch-ready experiment brief (no critical missing fields blocking launch)
expectations.evidence: All required fields present: hypothesis, control/test design, eligibility, metrics, guardrails, success threshold, duration, stopping logic, and decision rules. Brief is structured and actionable.

expectations.text: Output includes all required structural sections: hypothesis, variants (control + test), target audience with eligibility criteria, primary metric, secondary metrics, guardrails, success threshold, stopping logic, and decision rules
expectations.evidence: Sections 1-9 cover: hypothesis (section 1), control+test variants (section 2), target audience with eligibility (section 3), primary metric CTR (section 4), secondary metrics DAU/MAU and opt-out rate (section 5), guardrails (section 6), success threshold (section 7), stopping logic (section 8), and decision rules (section 9).

expectations.text: Output correctly captures the eligibility requirement (≥7 days of activity history required for smart-send model)
expectations.evidence: Section 3 explicitly states 'Minimum 7 days of app activity history (required to establish reliable historical activity patterns for the send-time model)' and in section 2 notes that peak activity is 'determined by analyzing the past 7 days of app session data'.

expectations.text: Output includes at least one operational or validity risk specific to this test (e.g., novelty effect, model accuracy dependency, delivery timing variance, or exposure bias from users with no history)
expectations.evidence: Section 10 identifies four operational risks: (1) Data & Model Dependency—'Success depends on the accuracy of the historical activity model'; (2) Novelty Effect—'Initial uplift may include a novelty boost from personalized timing; monitor decay'; (3) Timezone Handling—risk of late-night sends; (4) Cohort Stability. These directly address model accuracy and novelty bias.

expectations.text: Output defines distinct outcomes and follow-on actions for success, partial result (5–9% uplift), and failure
expectations.evidence: Section 9 decision framework clearly maps three outcomes: (1) Success: 'CTR ≥+10% and guardrails healthy → Full rollout'; (2) Partial (5–9%): 'Retest with refined model'; (3) Failure: 'CTR ≤0% or opt-out rate increases materially → Archive; investigate friction points; do not roll out'.
